fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List, locate the target CLB instance, and click Configure in the Health Status column.
3. For each listener exposing high risk or unnecessary ports:
• Delete the listener if not required, or
• Modify the listener to use only organization-approved service ports.
4. To create a listener, click Create. Select a protocol, enter a port number (only service ports are allowed), and click OK.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List and click the link of a desired instance.
3. Click the Listener Management tab for each listener configured on the CLB instance:
• Review the listening port and identify any ports classified as high-risk (for example, SSH, RDP, and database ports).
• Verify that only necessary public service ports are exposed to the internet.

Rule.title: Ensure that No CLB Listeners Allow Ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to Non-Service Ports
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that Cloud Load Balancer (CLB) instances do not allow unrestricted (0.0.0.0/0) access to non-service ports. CLB listeners and access control settings should be configured so that only required service ports (for example, 80 and 443, or other approved application ports) are accessible, and non-service or internal ports are not exposed to all IP address ranges.

Rationale:
Allowing all IP addresses (0.0.0.0/0) to access non-service ports on CLB instances increases the attack surface and exposes internal or sensitive services to malicious scanning and exploitation attempts. Applying an allowlist based on the principle of least privilege ensures that only trusted sources can reach specific ports, thereby reducing the risk of network attacks and unauthorized access.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List and click Configure in the Health Status column.
3. Remove unrestricted access to non-service ports.
4. Click Create. Select a protocol, enter a port number (only service ports are allowed), and click OK.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List and click the link of a desired instance.
3. Choose Listener Management and verify that non-service ports in the listener are not open to all IP addresses.

Rule.title: Ensure that the Certificate Associated with CLB Is Within the Validity Period
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Certificates managed within the CLB service should be monitored for expiration and removed or updated promptly once they expire.

Rationale:
Ensure that the certificate associated with the CLB is within its validity period to reduce service interruptions caused by certificate expiration and prevent situations where users cannot access the website normally.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose Certificate Management.
3. For each expired or about to expire certificate:
• Click Update on the right of the corresponding certificate.
• In the displayed Update Certificate dialog box, complete the required certificate information.
• Click Update to replace the certificate.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose Certificate Management.
3. In the certificate list, locate the Expiration At column for each certificate.
4. Verify that:
• Each certificate is currently valid.
• The remaining validity period meets the organization certificate management policy (e.g. the certificate is valid for at least 15 days).

Rule.title: Ensure that CFS File Systems Are Associated with Permission Groups According to the Principle of Least Privilege
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that each Cloud File Storage (CFS) file system is associated with an appropriate permission group and that the permission group rules are configured according to the principle of least privilege. Only trusted IP address ranges should be allowed to access required service ports, and unnecessary or overly broad access (for example, allowing all IP addresses) must be avoided.

Rationale:
CFS permission groups function as virtual firewalls controlling network access to file systems. Configuring allowlist rules based on the principle of least privilege helps to:
• Limit access to only trusted IP address ranges and required ports.
• Reduce exposure to malicious or unauthorized access attempts.
• Lower the risk of data leakage, tampering, or abuse of shared file resources.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
Creating a New Permission Group 1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud File Storage.
2. Go to Permission Group and click Create.
3. Enter a permission group name and remarks and click OK.
4. Click the newly created permission group and then click Add Rule to:
• Allow only trusted IP address ranges.
• Restrict access to the minimum required ports and protocols.
Associating a New Permission Group with the CFS File System 1. Go to File System List and click the ID for the target CFS file system.
2. Click Mount Point Info, locate Permission Group, and select the appropriate permission group.
3. Click Save.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud File Storage.
2. Choose File System List and click the file system ID to be reviewed to open its details page.
3. Click Mount Point Info and verify that for every mount point:
• A permission group is configured within the Permission Group parameter.
• The associated permission group's rules comply with the principle of least privilege (e.g. only trusted IP address ranges are allowed and only required service ports are open).

Rule.title: Ensure that Redis® Is Associated with a Security Group Configured with Least-privilege Network Access Rules
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that each CloudDB for Redis® instance is associated with an appropriate security group and the security group rules are configured according to the principle of least privilege. Only trusted IP address ranges should be allowed to access the required Redis service ports, and broad or unnecessary access (for example, allowing all IP addresses) must be avoided.

Rationale:
Security groups act as virtual firewalls controlling network traffic to and from Redis® instances. Configuring allowlist rules based on the principle of least privilege helps to:
• Restrict access to only trusted IP addresses ranges and required ports.
• Reduce exposure to malicious or unauthorized access attempts.
• Lower the risk of data leakage, data tampering, or service abuse.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
Creating a Security Group:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. In the navigation pane, choose Security Group.
3. Click Create, select Custom for Template, enter a security group name, and click OK.
4. Click Set Rules Now and configure rules as follows:
• Add default deny rules so that access from all IP addresses to all ports is blocked by default.
• Add allow rules for trusted IP address ranges and the required service ports based on business needs.
Associating the Security Group with the Instance:
1. For new instances, during creation, select an existing or newly created security group to associate with the instance.
2. For existing instances, go to CloudDB for Redis® > Instance List, locate the target instance, click More > Security Group, and select the appropriate security groups.
3. Click OK to save the configuration.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to CloudDB for Redis®.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the corresponding instance, and click More on the right.
3. Click Security Group and verify that:
• At least one security group is associated with the instance.
• The rules in the associated security groups comply with the principle of least privilege (e.g. only trusted IP address ranges are allowed and only required service ports are open).

Rule.title: Ensure that No Security Groups Allow Ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to Remote Server Administration Ports
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that security groups do not contain overly permissive inbound rules (for example, allowing all IP ranges such as 0.0.0.0/0 or all ports). Overly broad security group rules can expose internal services directly to the internet and significantly increase the risk of unauthorized access and attack.

Rationale:
Security groups act as virtual firewalls controlling network traffic to and from cloud resources. Applying the principle of least privilege to security group rules helps to:
• Prevent unrestricted exposure of services to the public internet.
• Limit access to trusted IP address ranges and required ports only.
• Reduce the likelihood of malicious scanning, exploitation, or unauthorized access.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Security Group and click on the target security group to enter its details page.
3. On the Inbound Rule tab, identify any rule that:
• Allows all IP ranges (for example, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0).
• Grants access to all ports or unnecessary ports.
4. Delete or modify such rules as follows:
• Replace overly broad IP ranges with specific trusted IP address ranges or subnets.
• Restrict allowed ports to only the required service ports.
5. Save the updated security group configuration and confirm that no inbound rule allows unrestricted access from all IP ranges.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. For each security group to be reviewed, click on the security group name to enter its details page.
3. Review all inbound rules and verify that:
• No rule allows all IP ranges (for example, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0) to access all ports.
• Where public access is required, rules are restricted to specific IP ranges and necessary service ports only.

Rule.title: Ensure that No Security Groups Allow Ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to Non-Service Ports
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that security group rules do not allow open access from all IP segments (for example, 0.0.0.0/0) to non-service ports on CVM instances. Security groups act as virtual firewalls and should be configured according to the principle of least privilege so that only trusted IP addresses and required service ports are allowed.

Rationale:
Restricting inbound access in security groups to only necessary service ports and trusted IP ranges helps prevent exposure of internal or administrative ports (for example, database or management ports) to the public internet, reduces the attack surface available to malicious scanners and exploit attempts, and limits the impact of unauthorized access attempts, thereby improving overall network security for CVM instances.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Security Group and click on the security group ID or name to go to its details page.
3. On the Inbound Rule tab, identify any rule that:
• Uses 0.0.0.0/0 (or equivalent "any" IP range), and
• Allows access to non-service ports or a wide range of ports (for example, all ports).
4. Modify or delete such rules as follows:
• Restrict the allowed ports to only necessary service ports; and
• Where possible, replace 0.0.0.0/0 with specific trusted IP address ranges or subnets.
5. Save the updated security group configuration and confirm that no inbound rule permits open access from all IP segments to non-service ports.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Security Group.
3. For each security group associated with CVM instances, click on the security group ID or name to open its details page.
4. Click the Inbound Rule tab.
5. Verify that:
• There are no inbound rules that allow 0.0.0.0/0 (or other "any" IP ranges, such as ::/0) to access non-service ports.
• Any rules using 0.0.0.0/0 are strictly limited to approved public service ports only (for example, HTTP/HTTPS if required by business needs).

Rule.title: Ensure Default Domain Names Are Set for HTTP/HTTPS Listeners
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that a default domain (Default Server) is configured for each HTTP/HTTPS listener on CLB instances. When a client request does not match any configured domain name for that listener, CLB forwards the request to the default domain. By defining forwarding rules for the default domain, unmatched or potentially illegitimate requests can be directed to a blackhole route or other non-sensitive target, preventing them from reaching backend real servers (RS).

Rationale:
Configuring a default domain for CLB listeners ensures that requests with unmatched or malformed host headers are not accidentally routed to production backend servers.
Redirecting such traffic to a blackhole route or controlled endpoint reduces the risk of unauthorized access, information leakage, or misuse of backend services caused by unexpected or malicious requests.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List. Locate the CLB instance to be reviewed and click its ID to go to the details page.
3. Click Listener Management.
4. In the HTTP/HTTPS Listener area:
• If there are no listeners, create an HTTP/HTTPS listener as required.
• For each HTTP/HTTPS listener, enable the default domain feature (for example, set Default Domain Name to Enable).
• Configure a default domain name and define forwarding rules so that unmatched or illegal requests are sent to a blackhole route or an appropriate non-sensitive target backend.
5. Save the configuration and verify that exactly one default domain is configured per listener and that its behavior aligns with security requirements.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Load Balancer.
2. Choose LB Instance List. Locate the CLB instance to be reviewed and click its ID to go to the details page.
3. Click Listener Management.
4. In the HTTP/HTTPS Listener area, for each HTTP/HTTPS listener:
• Verify that the default domain name has been configured.
• Review the forwarding rule for the default domain and confirm that unmatched/illegal requests are not directed to production backend RS.

Rule.title: Ensure that No Network ACLs Allow Ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to Remote Server Administration Ports
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that network ACLs associated with subnets do not contain inbound rules that allow unrestricted traffic from any source. Inbound rules that permit all protocols and all ports from 0.0.0.0/0 (action: Allow) expose the subnet to unnecessary risk and broad external access. Network ACLs should be configured according to the principle of least privilege, allowing only required traffic from trusted IP ranges.

Rationale:
Network ACLs provide subnet-level access control. Allowing all inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 removes meaningful access restrictions and increases the likelihood of malicious scanning, exploitation, and unauthorized access to resources within the subnet. Restricting inbound rules to specific protocols, ports, and trusted source IP ranges (allowlist model) aligns with the principle of least privilege and reduces the attack surface for workloads hosted in the VPC.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Go to Subnet. Locate and click the target subnet to open the subnet details page.
3. Click the ACL Rule tab.
4. Identify any inbound rule that allows all traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 (for example, all protocols and all ports with action = Allow).
5. Delete such overly permissive inbound rules, or modify them to:
• Limit the rule to only required service ports and protocols.
• Restrict the source to specific trusted IP addresses or CIDR ranges.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Choose Subnet. Locate and click the subnet to be reviewed to open the subnet details page.
3. Click the ACL Rule tab (or equivalent network ACL configuration view).
4. Review the inbound rules and verify that:
• No rule allows all traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 (for example, all protocols, all ports, action = Allow).
• Inbound rules are restricted to required protocols, ports, and trusted source IP ranges.

Rule.title: Ensure that No Network ACLs Allow Ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to Non-Service Ports
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that network ACLs associated with subnets do not contain overly permissive inbound rules for non-service ports. For the purpose of this control, service ports are defined as TCP ports 80 and 443. Any inbound rule that allows traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 to ports other than 80 and 443 with action Allow can unnecessarily expose the subnet and its assets to the public network and is considered non-compliant.

Rationale:
Network ACLs provide subnet-level access control. Allowing unrestricted inbound access from 0.0.0.0/0 to non-service ports exposes internal services to scanning, exploitation, and unauthorized access. Configuring inbound rules according to the principle of least privilege — restricting traffic to required service ports and trusted source IP ranges — reduces the attack surface and lowers the risk of malicious activity against workloads in the VPC.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Choose Subnet. Locate and click the target subnet to open the subnet details page.
3. Click ACL Rule to view the associated network ACL rules.
4. Identify any inbound rule that:
• Has source 0.0.0.0/0.
• Allows traffic to ports other than 80 and 443 with action Allow.
5. For each such rule, either:
• Delete the rule; or
• Modify the rule to limit access to required service ports only and/or restrict the source to trusted IP addresses or CIDR ranges.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Choose Subnet. Locate and click the subnet to be reviewed to open the subnet details page.
3. Click ACL Rule to view the associated network ACL rules.
4. Review the inbound rules and verify that:
• No rule allows traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 to ports other than 80 and 443 with action Allow.
• Inbound access to any non-service ports is restricted to specific trusted IP addresses or CIDR ranges, as required by business needs.

Rule.title: Ensure that Connectivity from VPC to Underlay Network Is Governed by Least-privilege Access Controls
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that access from VPC networks to the Underlay network (for example, to public services or PaaS products deployed in the Underlay) is explicitly controlled and limited to the minimum required scope. Access policies must restrict the VPCs, subnets, destination VIPs, and ports according to specific business requirements, rather than allowing broad or unrestricted connectivity.

Rationale:
Access mappings from VPC networks to the Underlay network extend the reachable attack surface beyond the VPC itself. Configuring these mappings according to the principle of least privilege — limiting which VPCs and subnets can access which Underlay services and ports — helps prevent unauthorized access, lateral movement, and abuse of shared Underlay services. Tight control over these routes and ports improves overall network segmentation and reduces the risk of misconfiguration leading to unintended exposure.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the operation console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Choose Physical Network Service Mapping.
3. For any existing rule that is broader than necessary:
• Edit the rule to restrict the VPC, subnet, VIP, and port(s) to only what is required by the business; or
• Delete the rule if it is no longer needed.
4. To create a new least-privilege mapping rule:
• Click Create in Physical Network Service Mapping.
• In the dialog box, select the specific VPC, subnet, VIP, and port(s) required for the connection.
• Confirm and save the rule.
5. For PaaS services, after the mapping rule is created, use the VPC API to associate the mapped resources with appropriate security groups to enforce fine- grained access control on top of the route.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the operation console and navigate to Virtual Private Cloud.
2. Go to Physical Network Service Mapping to view all configured VPC – Underlay mappings.
3. For each mapping rule, verify that:
• Only the required VPCs and subnets are included.
• The mapped VIP and ports correspond only to business-required public services or PaaS products.
• No overly broad rules exist (for example, wide VPC ranges or unnecessarily open port ranges that are not justified by business needs).

Rule.title: Ensure that Scheduled Snapshot Policies Are Configured for CBS Volumes
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>It is recommended that automatic scheduled snapshot policies are configured for CBS volumes according to their business criticality. Periodic creation of snapshots improves data durability and supports low-cost, high-efficiency disaster recovery.

Rationale:
Enabling scheduled snapshots for CBS volumes enhances data protection and disaster recovery capabilities. Regular snapshots help minimize data loss and reduce business downtime by providing multiple recovery points in the event of accidental deletion, corruption, or infrastructure failures.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Block Storage.
2. Locate the CBS volume that requires a scheduled snapshot policy and, in the Operation column, choose More > Set Scheduled Snapshot Policy.
3. Click Create Policy, configure the schedule (for example, execution time, frequency, and retention period) according to business and recovery requirements, and click OK.
4. Click Set Scheduled Snapshot Policy again, select the newly created policy, and click OK to associate it with the target volume.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Cloud Block Storage.
3. For each CBS volume in scope, verify that:
• A scheduled snapshot policy is associated with the volume; and
• The policy schedule (frequency and retention) meets organizational backup and recovery requirements.

Rule.title: Ensure that Scheduled Snapshot Policies Are Configured for Core CBS Volumes
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that automatic scheduled snapshots are enabled for core Cloud Block Storage (CBS) volumes (for example, system disks or critical data disks). Periodic snapshots improve data security and support low-cost, high-availability disaster recovery for key workloads.

Rationale:
Enabling scheduled snapshots for core CBS volumes enhances data protection and disaster recovery capabilities. Regular snapshots help minimize data loss and reduce business downtime in the event of accidental deletion, data corruption, or infrastructure failures.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Block Storage.
2. Locate the core CBS volume that requires a scheduled snapshot policy and, in the Operation column, click More > Set Scheduled Snapshot Policy.
3. Click Create Policy, configure the schedule (for example, backup cycle, backup date, backup time, and retention type) according to business and recovery requirements, and click OK.
4. Click Set Scheduled Snapshot Policy again, select the newly created policy, and click OK to associate it with the target core volume.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. In the navigation pane, choose Cloud Block Storage.
3. Identify CBS volumes classified as core (for example, volumes attached to production or critical systems).
4. For each core CBS volume, verify that:
• A scheduled snapshot policy is associated with the volume; and
• The policy schedule (frequency and retention) meets organizational backup and recovery requirements.

Rule.title: Ensure that Encryption Is Enabled for CBS
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that Cloud Block Storage (CBS) volumes are encrypted to protect data at rest.
Encrypted volumes help prevent unauthorized access, data leakage, and tampering, thereby strengthening the confidentiality and integrity of stored data.

Rationale:
Enabling encryption for CBS volumes improves data security by ensuring that data at rest cannot be accessed or modified by unauthorized parties. Encryption mitigates risks such as data leakage, unauthorized retrieval, and exposure arising from improper handling or compromised storage resources.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Block Storage.
2. Click Create to create a new CBS volume.
3. In the displayed dialog box, select Enable Cloud Disk Encryption, choose an appropriate encryption method, and click OK.
4. For existing unencrypted volumes, create a new encrypted volume and migrate data according to operational requirements, as encryption cannot be enabled directly on an existing unencrypted disk.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. In the navigation pane, choose Cloud Block Storage.
3. Locate the target CBS volume and click its ID/name.
4. Click the Parameter tab, locate the Encrypt parameter, and verify that:
• The encryption feature is enabled.
• The selected encryption algorithm meets organizational security requirements.

Rule.title: Ensure that CBS Volumes Are Properly Mounted to Their Associated Instances
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>All CBS volumes should be in their expected state (either mounted to the correct CVM instance or intentionally unmounted for maintenance/migration). Unmounted or abnormally mounted volumes may cause data inaccessibility, instance startup failures, or service interruptions.

Rationale:
Regularly checking CBS mounting status helps prevent issues such as data loss, service degradation, or operational failures. Early detection of abnormal or unmounted volumes reduces the risk of service disruption and supports stable system operations.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Block Storage.
2. For any volume not in a normal mounted state, remount the disk to the corresponding CVM instance based on operational requirements.
3. If mounting fails, troubleshoot underlying system issues (for example, instance configuration, permissions, or disk health) and retry the mounting operation.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. In the navigation pane, choose Cloud Block Storage.
3. Review the mounting status of each CBS volume and verify that:
• All expected volumes are mounted to their corresponding instances; and
• No volumes are in an abnormal or detached state.

Rule.title: Ensure that CFS File Systems Are in a Normal Operating State
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>CFS file systems should be monitored and confirmed to be in a normal operating state.
Abnormal file systems may result in access failures, data corruption, or service interruption for workloads dependent on shared file storage.

Rationale:
Regular monitoring of CFS file system status helps prevent data loss, access disruptions, and operational instability. Early identification of abnormal states reduces the likelihood of service outages and supports reliable and secure file operations.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and choose Cloud File Storage.
2. Identify any file system not in a normal state and review detailed status information.
3. Perform corrective actions such as troubleshooting configuration issues, repairing file system health, or engaging support if necessary.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud File Storage.
In the navigation pane, choose File System List.
2. Verify that:
• Each file system is in a normal state; and
• No file system is reporting errors, degraded status, or abnormal performance conditions.

Rule.title: Ensure that Server-Side Encryption Is Enabled for COS Buckets
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that server-side encryption is enabled for Cloud Object Storage (COS) buckets.
Server-side encryption protects data at rest by automatically encrypting objects upon upload and decrypting them during access, reducing the risk of unauthorized access or data exposure.

Rationale:
Enabling server-side encryption ensures that data stored in COS buckets is encrypted before being written to disk, enhancing confidentiality and reducing the likelihood of data leakage resulting from unauthorized access or misconfigurations.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, click its name, and go to the details page.
3. Choose Security Management > Server-Side Encryption, click Modify, select the required encryption method (SSE-COS or SSE-KMS), and click Save.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, and click Configuration Management.
3. In the navigation pane, choose Security Management > Server-Side Encryption, and verify that:
• Server-side encryption is enabled; and
• Encryption Method is set to SSE-COS or SSE-KMS.

Rule.title: Ensure that Cross-Region Replication Is Enabled for COS Buckets
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that cross-region replication is enabled for Cloud Object Storage (COS) buckets.
Cross-region replication automatically and asynchronously copies new and updated objects — including metadata and version information — from a source bucket to a destination bucket in another region. Replication helps maintain identical object copies and supports disaster recovery by ensuring data redundancy across geographically separated locations.

Rationale:
Enabling cross-region replication enhances data durability and disaster recovery readiness. Maintaining synchronized replicas across regions reduces the risk of data loss and helps minimize service disruption during regional failures, outages, or accidental deletions.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, and click its name go to the details page.
3. Choose Fault Tolerance and Disaster Recovery Management > Versioning, click Modify, enable Current Status, and click Save.
4. Choose Bucket Replication. Under Inter-Cloud Replication or Cross- Cloud Replication, click Add Rule, specify the destination bucket and required configuration, and click OK.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, and click its bucket name to go to the details page.
3. Choose Fault Tolerance and Disaster Recovery Management > Bucket Replication and verify that:
• Cross-region replication is enabled; and
• At least one rule exists under Inter-Cloud Replication or Cross-Cloud Replication.

Rule.title: Ensure that Public Access Is Disabled for COS Buckets
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that Cloud Object Storage (COS) buckets do not allow public read or public read/write access. Public access settings permit anonymous users to read or modify bucket data, resulting in significant data exposure and integrity risks. Buckets should be configured with private read/write permissions unless a specific, approved business need exists.

Rationale:
Restricting bucket access based on the principle of least privilege reduces the risk of unauthorized access, data leakage, and malicious tampering.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the bucket that needs to be configured, and click its bucket name or Configuration Management to go to the bucket management page.
3. Choose Permission Management > Bucket Access Permission.
4. Set Public Permission to Private Read/Write and save the configuration.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Object Storage.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the bucket that needs to be configured, and click its bucket name.
3. Choose Permission Management > Bucket Access Permission and verify that Public Permission is set to Private Read/Write.

Rule.title: Ensure that Server-Side Encryption Is Set to SSE-KMS for CSP Buckets with Full Access Permissions
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>For CSP buckets that are configured with full access permissions, it is strongly recommended to enable server-side encryption using KMS-managed keys (SSE-KMS).
Unencrypted sensitive data stored in buckets is at risk of unauthorized access, tampering, and regulatory non-compliance, especially when broad access controls are granted.

Rationale:
Buckets with full access permissions present a higher inherent risk of data exposure.
Enabling server-side encryption with a KMS key ensures that stored data remains protected even if access permissions are misconfigured or exposed. Encryption mitigates the risk of data leakage and strengthens overall data security posture.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Storage Private.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, and open its details page.
3. Choose Security Management > Server-Side Encryption, click Modify, set Encryption Method and Encryption Algorithm, and click Save.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Storage Private.
2. Choose Bucket List, locate the target bucket, and click its bucket name.
3. Choose Security Management > Server-Side Encryption and verify that Encryption Method is set to SSE-KMS (or SSE-COS, if permitted by policy).

Rule.title: Ensure that Automated Backups Are Enabled for MariaDB Instances
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that automated backups are enabled for MariaDB instances. Regular backups (for example, at least once per day) support data recovery in the event of accidental deletion, data corruption, or infrastructure failures.

Rationale:
Enabling automated backups improves the database's disaster recovery capability and helps minimize business downtime by ensuring that recent restorable data copies are always available.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to MariaDB (TDSQL).
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click Manage on the right of the corresponding instance to go to the instance details page.
3. In the Availability Info area, click Change Deployment Mode, select Multi-AZ for Target Deployment Mode, add a replica node, and choose a different region for the replica node.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to MariaDB (TDSQL).
2. Choose Instance List and verify that all instances are configured as one master and one replica or one master and multiple replicas.

Rule.title: Ensure that Automated Backups Are Enabled for TDSQL for MySQL
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that automated backups are enabled for TDSQL for MySQL instances. Regular backups (for example, at least once per day) protect against data loss caused by accidental deletion, data corruption, or system failures.

Rationale:
Automated backups enhance the database's disaster recovery capability and help minimize business downtime by ensuring that recent and recoverable data copies are always available.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content: TDSQL for MySQL enables automated backups by default. No configuration action is required unless settings have been manually modified. If necessary, adjust the backup schedule and retention period under Backup and Log Settings.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDSQL for MySQL.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click Manage.
3. Choose Backup and Restoration > Backup and Log Settings, and verify that:
• Automated backups are enabled.
• Backup execution time and storage time are correctly displayed and meet organizational requirements.

Rule.title: Ensure that Data Encryption Is Enabled for TDSQL for MySQL Instances
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Ensure that storage encryption is enabled for TDSQL for MySQL instances. Storage encryption protects data at rest and helps prevent unauthorized access, tampering, or exposure of sensitive information.

Rationale:
Enabling storage encryption enhances the confidentiality and integrity of data stored in TDSQL for MySQL by ensuring that all data written to disk is encrypted, reducing the risk of data leakage or modification resulting from unauthorized access.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDSQL for MySQL.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click Manage.
3. Navigate to Data Security > Data Encryption, toggle Encryption Status on, configure the required authorization options, and click OK to apply the settings.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDSQL for MySQL.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click Manage.
3. In the navigation pane, choose Data Security > Data Encryption, and verify that:
• Encryption Status is displayed as enabled.
• The associated key authorization configuration is valid.

Rule.title: Ensure that Automated Backups Are Enabled for TDSQL for PostgreSQL
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Verify that automatic backups are enabled for the TDSQL for PostgreSQL instance and that data is backed up at least once every 24 hours.

Rationale:
Regular automated backups strengthen database resilience by ensuring that data can be restored quickly and reliably in the event of corruption, accidental deletion, or system failure, thereby reducing business downtime.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDSQL for PostgreSQL.
2. In the navigation pane, click an instance list, locate the target instance, and click Management.
3. Click Backup, click Automatic Backup Settings, and configure the backup interval to once every 24 hours.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDSQL for PostgreSQL.
2. In the navigation pane, click an instance list, locate the target instance, and click Management.
3. Click Backup, click Backup List, and confirm that backups exist and are performed at 24-hour intervals.

Rule.title: Ensure that Automated Backups Are Enabled for Redis® Instances
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Verify that automatic backups are enabled for CloudDB for Redis® instances and that the backup cycle and retention period meet minimum requirements.

Rationale:
Automatic backups enhance service resilience by enabling rapid data restoration in cases of unavailability, corruption, or misoperations, thereby reducing business impact and downtime.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and choose CloudDB for Redis®.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click the corresponding instance ID.
3. Click Backup and Recovery.
4. Click Configure Automatic Backup, select Enable for Automatic Backup, and select values for Backup Cycle.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to CloudDB for Redis®.
2. Choose Instance List, locate the target instance, and click the instance ID.
3. Click Backup and Restoration, click Configure Automatic Backup, and verify that Automatic Backup is enabled, all days in Backup Cycle are selected, and the retention period exceeds 7 days.

Rule.title: Ensure that Scheduled Snapshot Policies Are Configured for CFS File Systems
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Verify that automatic periodic snapshots are enabled for CFS file systems to enhance data protection and support cost-effective disaster recovery.

Rationale:
Periodic snapshots strengthen data resilience by enabling rapid recovery from corruption, deletion, or service disruptions, thereby reducing business downtime.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud File Storage.
2. Choose Snapshot > Snapshot and Scheduled Snapshot Policy, click Create, enter a name, select all dates for Backup Date, configure an execution time, set a retention period greater than 7 days, and click OK.
3. For the newly created policy, click Associate File System, select the required file system, and click OK.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud File Storage.
2. Choose Snapshot > Snapshot and Scheduled Snapshot Policy and check whether file systems are associated with a valid policy.
3. Choose Snapshot List and confirm that there are snapshot records.

Rule.title: Ensure that Off-Cloud Storage Is Configured for BRMS
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>It is recommended to configure off-cloud storage for backup data managed by BRMS.
Verify that off-cloud storage is configured to ensure that backup copies are not stored solely within the cloud environment, thereby reducing the risk of data loss caused by cloud-level failures.

Rationale:
Storing backup data in a distributed manner strengthens data resilience and reduces the impact of regional or platform-level disruptions.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the BRMS console as an administrator and navigate to System Management from the top menu.
2. In the navigation pane, choose System Settings.
3. In the System Self-Backup area, click Edit.
4. On the Edit tab, configure Backup Execution Time, Backup Replica Storage Method, and Backup Storage as required.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the BRMS console and navigate to Backup Plan.
2. Click Related Information and click Backup Policy.
3. Under Backup Object, click View Details and verify that the resource set name is displayed.

Rule.title: Ensure that Backup Resource Sets Are Configured to Include All Critical Data in BRMS
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Verify that resource sets are correctly configured to ensure that backup tasks include all critical data and avoid incomplete backups.

Rationale:
Properly defining resource sets ensures that important data is included in routine backup tasks and supports ongoing maintenance of a complete sensitive data inventory.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the TCE operation console. Navigate to Platform OPS > High Availability Center > Backup Recovery Management System.
2. Choose Backup Plan. In the Related Information area, click Backup Policy. Locate Retention Policy, and click the edit icon.
3. In the Edit Retention Policy dialog box, toggle Retention Policy on and click Confirm.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the BRMS console and navigate to Backup Plan.
2. Click Related Information and click Backup Policy.
3. Locate the Retention Policy parameter and confirm that the data cleanup policy is properly configured.

Rule.title: Ensure that the Retention Policy Is Configured for Backup Policies in BRMS
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>If retention policies are not enabled, backup data will accumulate without cleanup. This may lead to storage exhaustion and subsequent backup failures.

Rationale:
Configurable retention periods help manage storage capacity and ensure that data is retained according to its importance and compliance requirements.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the TCE operation console. Navigate to Platform OPS > High Availability Center > Backup Recovery Management System.
2. Choose Backup Plan. In the List navigation pane, click Create.
3. On the Create Backup Plan page, set Backup Storage to Off-Cloud Storage.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the BRMS console and navigate to Backup Plan.
2. Click Related Information and click Backup Storage.
3. Verify that Storage Type is set to Off-Cloud Storage.

Rule.title: Ensure that CVM Instances Are Running Normally
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Abnormal CVM instance status may cause service disruption. Regular verification helps ensure that any anomalies are not caused by unexpected changes or failures.

Rationale:
Regularly checking the status of CVM instances helps reduce the risk of service interruption, data loss, or operational failures caused by system issues.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Instances and locate the affected instance.
3. If the instance status is abnormal:
• Review recent changes or events to identify potential causes.
• Reboot the instance if appropriate and confirm that it returns to Running status.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Cloud Virtual Machine.
2. Choose Instances, locate the target instance, and verify that its status is Running.

Rule.title: Ensure that Multi-level Approval Workflows Are Configured for High-Risk Operations
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Performing high-risk operations without prior approval may lead to operational mistakes that could affect system stability or service availability. Regular verification helps ensure that appropriate approval controls are in place.

Rationale:
Requiring approval for high-risk operations helps reduce the risk of service disruption, configuration errors, or unintended changes by ensuring that such actions are reviewed by designated approvers.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Approval Management.
2. On the Approval Workflow Management page, click New, and specify the workflow name and description.
3. Associate the workflow with approval businesses, toggle Enable Approval on, configure the approval flow with three or more nodes, and click Confirm.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Approval Management.
2. On the Approval Workflow Management page, click Edit for the target workflow and verify that three or more approval nodes are configured in the approval workflow.

Rule.title: Ensure that High-Risk Script and Command Detection Is Enabled
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Delivering high-risk commands (such as shutdown, reboot, or delete operations) through scripts without interception may result in unintended changes or service impact.
Verification is required to ensure that command detection and blocking rules are properly configured.

Rationale:
Enabling high-risk command detection helps prevent accidental or unauthorized execution of commands that may lead to service disruption, data loss, or other operational risks.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Application Operations Platform.
2. Choose Security Settings, click Create, and configure a rule to prohibit high- risk commands.
3. After completing the configuration, click Confirm to apply the rule.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Application Operations Platform.
2. Choose Security Settings and verify that rules prohibiting high-risk commands are enabled.

Rule.title: Ensure that Independent Roles and ACL Policies Are Configured for Producers and Consumers
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Lack of independent roles and granular access control for producers and consumers may lead to unauthorized access, data disorder, or invalid business data across Kafka topics.

Rationale:
Configuring distinct roles and ACL policies enforces permission isolation, supports multi-team collaboration, and upholds the principle of least privilege. This minimizes unauthorized operations and protects the integrity of messaging data.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for CKafka.
2. Choose Instance List, select the target instance, and go to User Management. Click Create to add a user and set credentials.
3. Navigate to ACL Policy Management, select the relevant resource, and edit the ACL policy to define allowed or denied read/write permissions for specific users or IP addresses.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for CKafka.
2. Choose Instance List, select the target instance, and go to User Management to verify that separate users are configured.
3. In the same instance, navigate to ACL Policy Management and confirm that ACL policies are configured to control read/write permissions for each topic.

Rule.title: Ensure that Independent Roles Are Configured for Producers and Consumers to Produce and Consume Different Namespace Resources
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Configuring independent roles for each producer and consumer can largely avoid issues such as data disorder and invalid business data caused by unclear permissions.

Rationale:
This mechanism effectively achieves permission isolation between different business units, ensuring the security of the messaging system while meeting resource management requirements in multi-team collaboration scenarios. By adhering to the principle of least privilege, it fundamentally avoids data disorder caused by unauthorized access.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for Apache Pulsar.
2. Choose Namespace, select a cluster, locate the target namespace, and click Configure Permission.
3. On the displayed page, click Add Role, and define the required production or consumption permissions.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for Apache Pulsar.
2. Choose Namespace, select a cluster, locate the target namespace, and click Configure Permission.
3. Verify that roles are configured with appropriate production and consumption permissions.

Rule.title: Ensure that Independent Roles Are Configured for Producers and Consumers to Produce and Consume Different Namespace Resources
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Absence of independent roles and granular permissions for producers and consumers may lead to unauthorized access, data disorder, or invalid business data within namespace resources.

Rationale:
Configuring separate roles with explicit production and consumption permissions enforces isolation between business units and supports the principle of least privilege.
This reduces the risk of unauthorized operations and helps maintain messaging integrity.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for Apache RocketMQ.
2. Choose Cluster Management, locate the target cluster, and go to its details page.
3. Click Namespace, click Configure Permission, and configure the required production and consumption permission policies for each role.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to TDMQ for Apache RocketMQ.
2. Choose Cluster Management, locate the target cluster, and go to its details page.
3. Click Namespace, click Configure Permission, and verify that roles are assigned appropriate production and consumption permissions.

Rule.title: Ensure that Distinct User Accounts and Permission Policies Are Configured for Producers and Consumers
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Lack of separate user accounts and explicit permissions for producers and consumers may lead to unauthorized access, data disorder, or invalid business data within designated cluster.

Rationale:
Configuring distinct user accounts with clearly defined permissions enforces isolation between different business units and supports the principle of least privilege. This reduces the risk of unauthorized operations and helps maintain the stability and integrity of messaging workloads.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the operation console and navigate to TDMQ for RabbitMQ.
2. Choose Cluster Management and Cluster List.
3. Click a target cluster and click User and Permission.
4. Create or update user accounts and configure the required permission policies for each producer and consumer.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the operation console and navigate to TDMQ for RabbitMQ.
2. Choose Cluster Management and Cluster List.
3. Click a target cluster and click User and Permission.
4. Verify that separate user accounts are created and that each user has the appropriate permissions for accessing and operating on designated cluster.

Rule.title: Ensure that Deployment Groups Are Isolated by Projects for Different Tenants
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Failure to isolate deployment groups across tenants may result in cross-tenant data exposure, resource contention, or unintended modification of tasks and workflows.

Rationale:
Associating deployment groups with projects ensures tenant-level separation of tasks and instances, reducing the risk of data leakage, operational interference, and permission misuse. This supports least-privilege access and enables clearer audit trails for tenant-specific operation.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Resource Management.
2. Create a project and authorize the required users.
3. When creating a deployment group in TCT, associate it with the project.
4. For existing deployment groups, transfer them into the appropriate project using resource management.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Resource Management.
2. Verify that a project has been created and that users are authorized appropriately.
3. When creating a deployment group in TCT, confirm that the deployment group is associated with a project.
4. For existing deployment groups, verify on the Resource Management page that they have been transferred into the appropriate project.

Rule.title: Ensure that Different Tenants or Services Are Isolated Through Transaction Grouping or DTF Cluster Configuration
Rule.description:
<VulnDiscussion>Lack of isolation between tenants or services may result in data exposure, transaction conflicts, resource contention, or difficulty attributing operational activities during audits.

Rationale:
Configuring transaction groups or DTF cluster isolation ensures that data, transactions, and resources are restricted to authorized tenants or services. This supports least- privilege access, prevents resource interference, and improves fault isolation and audit traceability.</VulnDiscussion>

reference.dc:title: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark
reference.dc:subject: CIS Tencent Cloud Enterprise Foundation Benchmark

fixtext.+content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Resource Management.
2. Create a project and authorize the required users.
3. In the DTF console, create a transaction group and associate it with the project.
4. Enable rate limiting for the transaction group.

check.check-content:
1. Log in to the tenant console and navigate to Resource Management.
2. Select a project and verify that appropriate users are authorized.
3. Navigate to the DTF console and choose Transaction Grouping.
4. For each transaction group:
• Verify that it is associated with a project.
• Confirm that only authorized users have access to the transaction group.
• Check whether rate limiting is enabled.
